profile.name: Akash Pathak
profile.location: Jaipur, India · open to relocate to Bengaluru

about: I'm a product-minded full-stack engineer who enjoys turning rough ideas into products people rely on. I start with the problem and the user, shape a clear plan, and then own the build end to end: interface, APIs, data and the pipeline that ships it.

Over about 2 years I've led a frontend team while owning backend services across a seven-product SaaS suite, moved services to Java 25 LTS, and kept systems fast and stable under real load. I care about clean design documents, honest code reviews, quick feedback loops and fixing problems at the root, and I'm quick to pick up new tools, including AI-assisted development.

job.tagline: I turn ideas into reliable, user-friendly products, owning the whole journey from problem and design to clean code, smooth releases and continuous improvement.

highlights.label: Products in a multi-app SaaS suite

points: Lead the frontend team across a suite of seven web and mobile products (LMS, Collection App, Customer App, API Box, Insights, Admin), while owning backend services end to end.
Upgraded backend services from Java 21 to the latest Java 25 LTS.
Built REST APIs and microservices in Java / Spring Boot, documented with OpenAPI / Swagger.
Designed Kafka event-driven notification services and integrated six third-party payment gateways with real-time status updates.
Kept services fast under heavy concurrent load with Redis caching, PostgreSQL query optimization and request-handling optimizations.
Built real-time features: live location tracking for field agents, live user-activity tracking, and a CloudFront CDN + Lambda layer for document delivery.
Shipped with Docker, Kubernetes (HPA autoscaling), Jenkins and Ansible, with deployment and test reports automated to email and Google Chat.
Resolved urgent production and performance issues in real time, tracing root causes across code, data and deployment.
Wrote system design documents before new features, reviewed them with the team, and ran Git-based code reviews.
